record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: stable matching probability under compact indifference
record.original_question: Under the compact-indifference model of uncertain preferences, what is the computational complexity of computing the probability that a given matching is stable in a Stable Marriage instance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with uncertain preferences under the compact-indifference model, defined as follows. There are n men and n women. Each agent specifies a weak preference order (a total preorder) over the agents of the opposite sex; ties in this weak order represent indifference. The realized preference of each agent is drawn independently and uniformly at random among all strict linear extensions of that agent's weak order. A matching M (a perfect matching between men and women) is stable for a given realization of strict preferences if no man-woman pair (m, w) both strictly prefer each other to their partners in M.

Given as input the weak preference order of each of the 2n agents and a perfect matching M, the StabilityProbability problem asks to compute the probability (over the independent uniform random linear extensions for all 2n agents) that M is a stable matching.

Determine the exact computational complexity of StabilityProbability under the compact-indifference model when both sides of the market may have uncertain (non-strict) preferences. In particular, is the problem #P-complete, polynomial-time solvable, or of intermediate complexity?
artifact.status_search_result: According to Aziz et al., "Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences" (Algorithmica, 2019), the complexity of computing StabilityProbability under the compact-indifference model when both sides are uncertain is explicitly left open. The polynomial-time case when one side has certain preferences is established (Theorem 8), but the general two-sided case remains unresolved as of the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences - PMC
status_evidence.snippet: StabilityProbability is open for the compact indifference model when both sides may be uncertain.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of StabilityProbability under the compact-indifference model with two-sided uncertainty is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences (arXiv:1607.02917)
status_evidence.snippet: We consider three uncertainty models including compact indifference and study the complexity of computing the stability probability.
status_evidence.claim: The compact-indifference model is defined and the StabilityProbability problem is the subject of study.
